@@ -0,0 +1,56 @@
+name: Glossary Terms
+
+# cycle-128 FR-6 (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-6.2, D-6.3): every backticked framework
+# term in the kernel (.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md) resolves to an entry or alias in
+# the framework glossary (.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md), or to an allowlisted code
+# identifier (.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt, at most 30 entries).
+# tools/check-glossary-terms.sh is the gate; the two control steps prove the
+# gate itself still bites. This check is Loa's own: it runs in this repository
+# only, never in a project that mounts the framework.
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+
+jobs:
+  glossary-terms:
+    name: Kernel terms resolve to the glossary
+    if: github.repository == '0xHoneyJar/loa'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout
+        # actions/checkout@v4.3.1 (pinned per cycle-098 supply-chain pattern)
+        uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5
+
+      - name: Check kernel terms against the glossary
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          bash tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --report
+          bash .claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh --type glossary --file .claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
+          bash .claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh --type glossary --file GLOSSARY.md
+
+      - name: Positive control (the gate rejects the miss fixture with exit 1)
+        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real failure above stays the visible failure
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          d=tests/fixtures/glossary/miss
+          rc=0
+          bash tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --kernel "$d/kernel.md" --glossary "$d/GLOSSARY.md" --allowlist "$d/allowlist.txt" || rc=$?
+          if [ "$rc" -ne 1 ]; then
+            echo "::error::check-glossary-terms.sh did not reject $d with exit 1 (got $rc)"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "OK: miss fixture rejected"
+
+      - name: Negative control (the gate accepts the ok fixture)
+        if: success()   # controls prove the gate bites; a real failure above stays the visible failure
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          d=tests/fixtures/glossary/ok
+          if ! bash tools/check-glossary-terms.sh --kernel "$d/kernel.md" --glossary "$d/GLOSSARY.md" --allowlist "$d/allowlist.txt"; then
+            echo "::error::check-glossary-terms.sh false-positive on $d"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "OK: ok fixture accepted"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/check-glossary-terms.sh: does every backticked framework term in the
+# kernel resolve to a glossary entry?
+#
+# The kernel (.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md) is the only extraction scope. Every
+# backticked span outside fenced code is a candidate; a span is kept only when
+# it matches ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$, which drops paths, scripts, flags,

+#                                 [--allowlist PATH] [--json] [--report]
+#
+#   --kernel PATH     default .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md
+#   --glossary PATH   default .claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
+#   --allowlist PATH  default .claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt
+#   --json            one JSON report on stdout
+#   --report          list every kept token with its resolution
+#                     (defined, alias, allowlisted or MISS)
+#
+# Exit codes: 0 every token resolves (a stale allowlist entry only WARNs)
+#             1 a token misses, or the allowlist has more than 30 entries
+#             2 usage, or an input file is unreadable
+# =============================================================================

+export LC_ALL=C
+
+usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
+
+ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+KERNEL="$ROOT/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+GLOSSARY="$ROOT/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
+ALLOWLIST="$ROOT/.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt"
+ALLOWLIST_MAX=30
+JSON=0
+REPORT=0
+ME="check-glossary-terms.sh"
+
+need_arg() { [[ $2 -ge 2 ]] || { echo "$ME: $1 needs a path" >&2; exit 2; }; }
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --kernel)    need_arg "$1" $#; KERNEL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --glossary)  need_arg "$1" $#; GLOSSARY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --allowlist) need_arg "$1" $#; ALLOWLIST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --json)   JSON=1; shift ;;
+    --report) REPORT=1; shift ;;
+    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "$ME: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+for f in "$KERNEL" "$GLOSSARY" "$ALLOWLIST"; do
+  [[ -f "$f" && -r "$f" ]] || { echo "$ME: cannot read $f" >&2; exit 2; }
+done
+if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
+  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "$ME: --json needs jq" >&2; exit 2; }
+fi
+
+# Display names: repo-relative when the file sits under the repo root.

+WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-glossary-terms.XXXXXX")"

+  /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
+  fence { next }

+    s = $0

+      s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH)

+    }
+  }

+#    the **Term** the name belongs to. Only the "## Language" section counts.

+  /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
+  fence { next }

+  /^# / { lang = 0; next }
+  !lang { next }
+  /^\*\*[^*]+\*\*:/ {
+    t = $0; sub(/^\*\*/, "", t); sub(/\*\*:.*$/, "", t); gsub(/`/, "", t)
+    gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", t)

+  }

+    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
+      p = parts[i]; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", p)

+    }
+  }

+#    ("MISS" with an empty entry when nothing matches), then

+#    longer occur in the kernel and "REDUNDANT<TAB>…<TAB>entry" for ones the
+#    glossary already resolves.

+  # a plural name, its singular (the plural fold is applied here only)
+  function add(map, x, v) { x = norm(x); put(map, x, v); put(map, x "s", v); put(map, x "es", v)

+                            if (x ~ /s$/) put(map, substr(x, 1, length(x) - 1), v) }

+  FILENAME == ARGV[2] { allow[norm($2)] = $1; allowtok[norm($2)] = $2; next }
+  {
+    used[norm($2)] = 1
+    if ((e = lookup(term, $2)) != "") r = "defined"
+    else if ((e = lookup(alias, $2)) != "") r = "alias"
+    else if (norm($2) in allow) { r = "allowlisted"; e = "" }
+    else { r = "MISS"; e = "" }
+    printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", r, $2, $1, e
+  }
+  END {
+    for (k in allow) {
+      if (!(k in used)) printf "STALE\t%s\t%s\t\n", allowtok[k], allow[k]
+      else if ((e = lookup(term, allowtok[k])) != "" || (e = lookup(alias, allowtok[k])) != "")
+        printf "REDUNDANT\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", allowtok[k], allow[k], e
+    }
+  }
+' "$WORK/names.tsv" "$WORK/allow.tsv" "$WORK/tokens.tsv" > "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+
+kept="$(wc -l < "$WORK/tokens.tsv" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
+allow_count="$(wc -l < "$WORK/allow.tsv" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
+n_of() { awk -F'\t' -v k="$1" '$1 == k' "$WORK/resolved.tsv" | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]'; }
+n_def="$(n_of defined)"; n_alias="$(n_of alias)"; n_allow="$(n_of allowlisted)"; n_miss="$(n_of MISS)"
+
+violations=()
+warnings=()
+while IFS=$'\t' read -r r tok ln entry; do
+  case "$r" in
+    MISS) violations+=("MISS: \`$tok\` ($DK:$ln) has no glossary entry; define **$tok** in $DG, add it to an entry's _Aliases_: line, or, if it is a code identifier, allowlist it in $DA with a '# reason' comment") ;;
+    STALE) warnings+=("allowlist entry '$tok' ($DA:$ln) no longer occurs in $DK; remove it") ;;
+    REDUNDANT) warnings+=("allowlist entry '$tok' ($DA:$ln) is already resolved by the glossary entry **$entry**; remove it") ;;
+  esac
+done < "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+if [[ "$allow_count" -gt "$ALLOWLIST_MAX" ]]; then
+  violations+=("the allowlist $DA has $allow_count entries, over the limit of $ALLOWLIST_MAX; define the framework terms among them in the glossary instead")
+fi
+
+if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
+  jq -Rn --arg kernel "$DK" --arg glossary "$DG" --arg allowlist "$DA" \
+     --argjson allow_count "$allow_count" --argjson allow_max "$ALLOWLIST_MAX" \
+     --rawfile v <(printf '%s\n' ${violations[@]+"${violations[@]}"}) \
+     --rawfile w <(printf '%s\n' ${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}) '
+    [inputs | split("\t") | {resolution: .[0], token: .[1], line: (.[2] | tonumber), entry: .[3]}] as $rows
+    | ($rows | map(select(.resolution | IN("defined", "alias", "allowlisted", "MISS")))) as $tokens
+    | {ok: null,
+       kernel: $kernel, glossary: $glossary, allowlist: $allowlist,
+       kept: ($tokens | length),
+       counts: {defined: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "defined")) | length),
+                alias: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "alias")) | length),
+                allowlisted: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "allowlisted")) | length),
+                missing: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "MISS")) | length)},
+       allowlist_entries: $allow_count, allowlist_max: $allow_max,
+       tokens: ($tokens | map({token, line, resolution, entry: (if .entry == "" then null else .entry end)})),
+       missing: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "MISS") | .token)),
+       stale_allowlist: ($rows | map(select(.resolution == "STALE") | .token)),
+       redundant_allowlist: ($rows | map(select(.resolution == "REDUNDANT") | .token)),
+       violations: ($v | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))),
+       warnings: ($w | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0)))}
+    | .ok = ((.violations | length) == 0)
+  ' < "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+else
+  if [[ "$REPORT" -eq 1 ]]; then
+    awk -F'\t' '$1 != "STALE" && $1 != "REDUNDANT" {
+      printf "%-11s %-24s line %-4s %s\n", $1, $2, $3, ($4 == "" ? "" : "-> " $4) }' "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+  fi
+  for w in ${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}; do echo "WARN: $w"; done
+  for v in ${violations[@]+"${violations[@]}"}; do echo "$v" >&2; done
+  echo "kernel tokens kept: $kept; defined: $n_def; alias: $n_alias; allowlisted: $n_allow; missing: $n_miss; allowlist entries: $allow_count/$ALLOWLIST_MAX"
+  if [[ ${#violations[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then echo "PASS"; else echo "FAIL" >&2; fi
+fi
+
+[[ ${#violations[@]} -eq 0 ]] || exit 1
+exit 0

+allow_count="$(wc -l < "$WORK/allow.tsv" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
+n_of() { awk -F'\t' -v k="$1" '$1 == k' "$WORK/resolved.tsv" | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]'; }
+n_def="$(n_of defined)"; n_alias="$(n_of alias)"; n_allow="$(n_of allowlisted)"; n_miss="$(n_of MISS)"
+
+violations=()
+warnings=()
+while IFS=$'\t' read -r r tok ln entry; do
+  case "$r" in
+    MISS) violations+=("MISS: \`$tok\` ($DK:$ln) has no glossary entry; define **$tok** in $DG, add it to an entry's _Aliases_: line, or, if it is a code identifier, allowlist it in $DA with a '# reason' comment") ;;
+    STALE) warnings+=("allowlist entry '$tok' ($DA:$ln) no longer occurs in $DK; remove it") ;;
+    REDUNDANT) warnings+=("allowlist entry '$tok' ($DA:$ln) is already resolved by the glossary entry **$entry**; remove it") ;;
+  esac
+done < "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+if [[ "$allow_count" -gt "$ALLOWLIST_MAX" ]]; then
+  violations+=("the allowlist $DA has $allow_count entries, over the limit of $ALLOWLIST_MAX; define the framework terms among them in the glossary instead")
+fi
+
+if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
+  jq -Rn --arg kernel "$DK" --arg glossary "$DG" --arg allowlist "$DA" \
+     --argjson allow_count "$allow_count" --argjson allow_max "$ALLOWLIST_MAX" \
+     --rawfile v <(printf '%s\n' ${violations[@]+"${violations[@]}"}) \
+     --rawfile w <(printf '%s\n' ${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}) '
+    [inputs | split("\t") | {resolution: .[0], token: .[1], line: (.[2] | tonumber), entry: .[3]}] as $rows
+    | ($rows | map(select(.resolution | IN("defined", "alias", "allowlisted", "MISS")))) as $tokens
+    | {ok: null,
+       kernel: $kernel, glossary: $glossary, allowlist: $allowlist,
+       kept: ($tokens | length),
+       counts: {defined: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "defined")) | length),
+                alias: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "alias")) | length),
+                allowlisted: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "allowlisted")) | length),
+                missing: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "MISS")) | length)},
+       allowlist_entries: $allow_count, allowlist_max: $allow_max,
+       tokens: ($tokens | map({token, line, resolution, entry: (if .entry == "" then null else .entry end)})),
+       missing: ($tokens | map(select(.resolution == "MISS") | .token)),
+       stale_allowlist: ($rows | map(select(.resolution == "STALE") | .token)),
+       redundant_allowlist: ($rows | map(select(.resolution == "REDUNDANT") | .token)),
+       violations: ($v | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))),
+       warnings: ($w | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0)))}
+    | .ok = ((.violations | length) == 0)
+  ' < "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+else
+  if [[ "$REPORT" -eq 1 ]]; then
+    awk -F'\t' '$1 != "STALE" && $1 != "REDUNDANT" {
+      printf "%-11s %-24s line %-4s %s\n", $1, $2, $3, ($4 == "" ? "" : "-> " $4) }' "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
+  fi
+  for w in ${warnings[@]+"${warnings[@]}"}; do echo "WARN: $w"; done
+  for v in ${violations[@]+"${violations[@]}"}; do echo "$v" >&2; done
+  echo "kernel tokens kept: $kept; defined: $n_def; alias: $n_alias; allowlisted: $n_allow; missing: $n_miss; allowlist entries: $allow_count/$ALLOWLIST_MAX"
+  if [[ ${#violations[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then echo "PASS"; else echo "FAIL" >&2; fi
+fi
+
+[[ ${#violations[@]} -eq 0 ]] || exit 1
+exit 0

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# .claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-7.5..D-7.7, §5.2) against small
+# fixture repositories built per test. Every case also asserts that `git worktree list` in the
+# fixture shows only the main tree afterwards and that the live tree was not touched.
+
+setup() {
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
+    SCRIPT="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh"
+    R="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/repo"
+    export TMPDIR="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/tmp"
+    mkdir -p "$R" "$TMPDIR"
+    export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
+    git -C "$R" init -q
+    git -C "$R" config user.email t@example.invalid
+    git -C "$R" config user.name t
+    git -C "$R" config commit.gpgsign false
+    # Base: a buggy add(); node_modules is ignored, as in a real project.
+    printf 'node_modules/\n.venv/\n' > "$R/.gitignore"
+    printf 'add() { echo $(( $1 - $2 )); }\n' > "$R/lib.sh"
+    commit "base"
+}
+
+commit() { git -C "$R" add -A && git -C "$R" commit -q -m "$1"; git -C "$R" rev-parse HEAD; }
+
+# The red test: asserts add 2 3 = 5 and prints what it got.
+add_red_test() {
+    mkdir -p "$R/tests"
+    cat > "$R/tests/test_add.sh" <<'EOF'
+. ./lib.sh
+got="$(add 2 3)"
+if [ "$got" = 5 ]; then echo "PASS add"; exit 0; fi
+echo "FAIL: add 2 3: expected 5, got $got"
+exit 1
+EOF
+}
+fix_lib() { printf 'add() { echo $(( $1 + $2 )); }\n' > "$R/lib.sh"; }
+
+# Status of the fixture after a run: only the main tree, no stash, the live tree as it was.
+assert_clean() {
+    local n
+    n="$(git -C "$R" worktree list | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
+    [ "$n" -eq 1 ] || { git -C "$R" worktree list; echo "worktrees left behind"; return 1; }
+    [ -z "$(git -C "$R" stash list)" ] || { echo "a stash was created"; return 1; }
+    [ -z "$(ls -A "$TMPDIR")" ] || { ls -la "$TMPDIR"; echo "scratch left behind"; return 1; }
+}
+
+rtc() { (cd "$R" && "$SCRIPT" "$@"); }
+
+@test "RTC-1 red fails by assertion, green passes: exit 0 VERIFIED with the red output printed" {
+    add_red_test; red="$(commit "test(bug): failing test")"
+    fix_lib; commit "fix(bug): add adds" >/dev/null
+    run rtc --red "$red" --test-file tests/test_add.sh -- sh tests/test_add.sh
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" == *"verdict: VERIFIED"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"--- red run (last 80 lines) ---"*"FAIL: add 2 3: expected 5, got -1"*"--- end red run ---"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" != *"WARN: no non-test file changed"* ]]
+    assert_clean
+}
+
+@test "RTC-2 a decoy that passes at both commits exits 3 DECOY" {
+    mkdir -p "$R/tests"; printf 'echo "PASS always"\nexit 0\n' > "$R/tests/test_decoy.sh"
+    red="$(commit "test: decoy")"
+    fix_lib; commit "fix" >/dev/null
+    run rtc --red "$red" -- sh tests/test_decoy.sh
+    [ "$status" -eq 3 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" == *"verdict: DECOY"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"PASS always"* ]]
+    assert_clean
+}
+
+@test "RTC-3 a --test-file absent at the red commit exits 4 NOT_A_RED before any worktree" {
+    printf 'x\n' > "$R/README"; red="$(commit "docs")"
+    add_red_test; fix_lib; commit "fix and test together" >/dev/null
+    run rtc --red "$red" --test-file tests/test_add.sh -- sh tests/test_add.sh
+    [ "$status" -eq 4 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" == *"does not exist at the red commit"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"verdict: NOT_A_RED"* ]]
+    assert_clean
+}
+
+@test "RTC-4 a red run that exits 127 (command not found) is NOT_A_RED, exit 4" {
+    mkdir -p "$R/tests"; printf 'rtc_no_such_command_xyz\n' > "$R/tests/test_missing.sh"
+    red="$(commit "test: calls a missing command")"
+    fix_lib; commit "fix" >/dev/null
+    run rtc --red "$red" -- sh tests/test_missing.sh
+    [ "$status" -eq 4 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" == *"verdict: NOT_A_RED"* ]]
+    assert_clean
+}
+
+@test "RTC-5 a bats file with a syntax error at red is NOT_A_RED, exit 4" {
+    local bats_bin="${BATS_ROOT:-}/bin/bats"
+    [ -x "$bats_bin" ] || bats_bin="$(command -v bats || true)"
+    [ -n "$bats_bin" ] || skip "no bats binary to run the fixture"
+    mkdir -p "$R/tests"
+    printf '@test "add" {\n  if [ 1 = 1 ]; then\n    true\n}\n' > "$R/tests/add.bats"
+    red="$(commit "test: broken bats file")"
+    printf '@test "add" {\n  . ./lib.sh\n  [ "$(add 2 3)" = 5 ]\n}\n' > "$R/tests/add.bats"
+    fix_lib; commit "fix" >/dev/null
+    run rtc --red "$red" -- "$bats_bin" tests/add.bats
+    [ "$status" -eq 4 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" == *"syntax error"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"verdict: NOT_A_RED"* ]]
+    assert_clean
+}
+
+@test "RTC-6 a pytest-style collection error in the red output is NOT_A_RED, exit 4" {
+    mkdir -p "$R/tests"
+    printf 'echo "ERROR collecting tests/test_add.py"\necho "ImportError while importing test module"\nexit 2\n' > "$R/tests/test_collect.sh"
+    red="$(commit "test: does not collect")"
+    fix_lib; printf 'exit 0\n' > "$R/tests/test_collect.sh"; commit "fix" >/dev/null
+    run rtc --red "$red" -- sh tests/test_collect.sh
+    [ "$status" -eq 4 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+    [[ "$output" == *"matched 'ERROR collecting'"* ]]
+    assert_clean
+}
+
+@test "RTC-7 a green that still fails exits 1 GREEN_FAILS and prints the green output" {

21:#                             (default fixed — an absent key is the shipped gate, envelope unchanged) and budget_cents_max

24:#                             the run refuses (exit 4, status budget_exceeded, reason budget). A malformed scale or maximum
25:#                             is said and fixed applies. With the key written the envelope's metadata carries
26:#                             budget_scale, budget_cents_effective, budget_cents_max.

36:#                             older: the previous round's, moved aside) or a pre-lock refusal (`workdir_unavailable`,
37:#                             `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed` — the previous envelope and
38:#                             sidecars go aside as `.prev`, never one `--since` shows newer); under the run lock, so a live run is refused (`refused_concurrent_run`, exit 2)

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

The skill's automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED rule for a missing walkthrough is not applied here because the task brief defines the PR description as the implementation report and asks for a merge verdict on the change itself; the verdict below rests on the code. **Complexity pass.** `validate_glossary()` is 74 lines (`head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:1253`), the same size as the existing `validate_map()` and a third of `validate_decisions()`; it is one awk program and follows the file's convention, so it is not blocked. `red-test-check.sh` keeps its helpers under 40 lines each. Over-engineering: the only shrinkable item is the fixture noted in Observation 9. net: -80 lines possible.

**Verdict:** APPROVED

---

## Observations

### 1. Validation false positive: abbreviations count as sentence ends

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:1297` — the sentence counter treats any `.`, `!` or `?` followed by whitespace as a sentence boundary, so a legitimate two-sentence definition containing `e.g. `, `i.e. ` or `etc. ` is rejected with exit 1.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:1297`
**Issue:** Reproduced: `**Eg**: A sample, e.g. this one. Another sentence here.` yields `the definition of "Eg" has 3 sentences; at most two` and the validator exits 1. The CI workflow runs this validator on both glossaries, so the false positive blocks a merge until the author rewrites around it.
**Suggestion:** Skip boundaries that follow a known abbreviation (`e\.g\.`, `i\.e\.`, `etc\.`, `vs\.`), or require the next non-space character to be an uppercase letter or digit before counting a boundary.
**Benefit:** Keeps the gate fail-closed on real three-sentence definitions without rejecting ordinary prose.

### 2. The kernel-term gate currently exercises no definition

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/tools/check-glossary-terms.sh:82` — the shape filter keeps only single-token spans, so every multi-word framework term in the kernel is dropped before resolution; on the live kernel the gate resolves 0 tokens to a defined term, 5 to aliases and 11 via the allowlist.
**File:** `head/tools/check-glossary-terms.sh:82`
**Issue:** The workflow header states the gate proves "every backticked framework term in the kernel resolves to an entry or alias". With the current shape, the 35 definitions in `head/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md` are never consulted for the real kernel; only five alias tokens (`br`, `RUNNING`, `HALTED`, `JACKED_OUT`, `LOA-VERDICT`) carry the positive path, and 11 of 16 kept tokens pass through the allowlist. A term that drifts between kernel and glossary (for example a renamed state) is caught only if it is a single backticked word. The allowlist also admits two ordinary English words, `full` and `ultra` (`head/.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt:8-9`), so any future backticked use of those words in the kernel passes unexamined.
**Suggestion:** Either extend the kept shape to spans of two or three capitalised or lowercase words (`^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*( [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*){0,2}$`) so terms such as `run mode` or `golden path` resolve when backticked, or document in the workflow header that the gate is a single-token drift check and that the glossary's own coverage is enforced by the validator alone.
**Benefit:** Makes the gate's reach match its stated contract, or makes the contract honest.

### 3. No CHANGELOG entry in the change set

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.github/workflows/check-glossary-terms.yml:1` — a new CI gate, a new artifact type, a new reviewer-facing script and two new glossaries ship with no `CHANGELOG.md` hunk anywhere in the 29-file diff.
**File:** `head/.github/workflows/check-glossary-terms.yml:1` (the first of the new user-visible surfaces)
**Issue:** The repository's own convention lists a `CHANGELOG [Unreleased]` entry among sprint deliverables (see the archived plan at `head/tests/fixtures/sprint-seams/cycle-127-sprint.md:30`). The documentation-verification step of this review treats a missing CHANGELOG entry per task as a gap. Confidence is medium because `CHANGELOG.md` is not among the touched files and this is part 3 of a sprint, so the entry may be planned for the closing part.
**Suggestion:** Add `[Unreleased]` lines for the glossary gate, the `glossary` artifact type, the seams rule with its 2026-10-13 cutoff, and `red-test-check.sh`.
**Benefit:** Operators discover the new date-gated plan requirement from the release notes rather than from a failing validator.

### 4. The green side runs even after the red side has already decided the verdict

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:313` — the green run is executed unconditionally before any red-side verdict is evaluated at line 318, so a red run that timed out (default 600 s) or passed (DECOY) is followed by a full green run whose result is then discarded.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:313`
**Suggestion:** Evaluate the red-side verdicts (TIMEOUT, DECOY, NOT_A_RED) immediately after the red run and `finish` before launching the green worktree's test; the header already documents red-first judgment, so only the ordering changes.
**Benefit:** Halves the worst-case wall clock for the three red-side outcomes.

### 5. Path heuristic flags slash idioms in prose

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:1288` — the path pattern matches any `word/word`, so `I/O`, `read/write` or `and/or` in a definition produce the "a path or file extension" WARN.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:1288`
**Suggestion:** Require at least one `.` or a second `/` in the match, or a leading `./`, `~/` or a known directory name, before warning.
**Benefit:** Fewer spurious WARN lines in CI logs for both glossaries.

### 6. Allowlist lines silently keep only their first token

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/tools/check-glossary-terms.sh:114` — an allowlist line such as `a_tok b_tok  # reason` registers only `a_tok`; `b_tok` is then reported as a MISS and `a_tok` as a stale entry, which points the author away from the real mistake.
**File:** `head/tools/check-glossary-terms.sh:114`
**Suggestion:** Exit 2 with a line-numbered message when a non-comment line holds more than one whitespace-separated field.
**Benefit:** The allowlist contract ("one token per line") becomes enforced rather than assumed.

### 7. Skill zone manifests do not cover the write the new instruction mandates

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/skills/discovering-requirements/SKILL.md:270` — the skill is told to create and update the repo-root `GLOSSARY.md`, but its declared writable zone is `grimoires/loa, .beads` (`head/.claude/skills/discovering-requirements/SKILL.md:30`); the same mismatch exists in `head/.claude/skills/designing-architecture/SKILL.md:206` versus `:25`.
**File:** `head/.claude/skills/discovering-requirements/SKILL.md:270`
**Suggestion:** Add the project glossary to each skill's `zones.state.paths`, or move the project glossary under `grimoires/loa/`. The runtime guard (`zone-write-guard.sh`) allows unclassified paths, so this is a manifest inconsistency rather than a blocked write today.
**Benefit:** The zone declaration stays a truthful description of what the skill writes.

### 8. SURGICAL: unrelated editorial trims in two skill files

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:223` — the Fast-Gate Parity sentence drops the `ruff format --check` and `mypy` examples; `head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:241` drops "regardless of other findings"; `head/.claude/skills/planning-sprints/SKILL.md:195` and `:205` reword bullets and remove the "Questions should demonstrate deep understanding" sentence. None of these serve the glossary, seams or red-test features.
**File:** `head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:223`
**Suggestion:** Keep wording-only edits out of a feature sprint, or restore the Python examples, which were the only non-JavaScript ones in that sentence.
**Benefit:** Smaller diff to review, and no silent loss of guidance for Python projects.

### 9. SIMPLICITY[shrink]: the seams fixture carries an entire archived plan

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/tests/fixtures/sprint-seams/cycle-127-sprint.md:70` — SEAMS-9 needs the header `**Date:**` and one `## Sprint` block without a seams table; the fixture copies 103 lines of review-round history, cost figures and bead ids that the test never reads.
**File:** `head/tests/fixtures/sprint-seams/cycle-127-sprint.md:70-96`
**Suggestion:** Cut the fixture to the header, the sprint block and the appendix (about 20 lines), keeping the real 2026-10-07 date.
**Benefit:** A fixture that a reader can see the point of; about 80 lines less to maintain.

### 10. Date gate reads a non-ISO date as "undated"

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:871` — the header date is extracted with a `YYYY-MM-DD` regex, so a plan with `**Date:** October 20, 2026` falls into the WARN-only branch and escapes the seams requirement.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:871`
**Suggestion:** Treat a `**Date:**` line that exists but does not parse as ISO as a violation ("date must be YYYY-MM-DD"), reserving the WARN for plans with no date line at all.
**Benefit:** The grandfathering rule cannot be satisfied by formatting.

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.github/workflows/check-glossary-terms.yml:35` and `:48` — the explicit `if: success()` on both control steps is GitHub Actions' default behaviour and changes nothing.
**File:** `head/.github/workflows/check-glossary-terms.yml:35`
**Suggestion:** Drop the two conditions and keep the comment, or keep them only if a future `continue-on-error` is planned.
**Benefit:** No reader wonders what the condition is guarding.

### 12. Output stripping leaves ANSI remnants

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:79` — `strip` deletes the ESC byte but not the `[31m` that follows it, so coloured test output reaches the tail and the JSON `red_tail` as `[31mFAIL[0m`.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:79`
**Suggestion:** Pass `TERM=dumb NO_COLOR=1` into the run, or strip `\033\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]` with `sed` before the control-character filter.
**Benefit:** Cleaner tails for the reviewer and for any consumer of the JSON.

**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:326` (exit-code gate) and `:52` (pattern list)

```

## Changes Required

### 1. Functionality: a test file absent at the red commit yields VERIFIED

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:326` — when the test file does not exist at the red commit, `sh` exits 2 with `cannot open`, `python3` exits 2 with `can't open file … No such file or directory` and `pytest` exits 4 with `file or directory not found`; none of these is 0, 126 or 127 and none matches an entry of `NOT_A_RED_PATTERNS` (`head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:52`), so the red side is accepted as an assertion failure and a passing green produces `verdict: VERIFIED`, exit 0.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:326` (exit-code gate) and `:52` (pattern list)
**Issue:** Reproduced twice in a fixture repo whose red commit predates the test and whose green commit adds test and fix together, which is exactly the discipline this tool exists to catch:

```
$ red-test-check.sh --red <pre-test commit> -- sh tests/test_add.sh
--- red run (last 80 lines) ---
sh: 0: cannot open tests/test_add.sh: No such file
verdict: VERIFIED          (exit 0)

$ red-test-check.sh --red <pre-test commit> -- python3 tests/test_add.py

verdict: VERIFIED          (exit 0)

`--test-file` (D-7.6) would catch this, but it is optional and both prescribed invocations omit it: `head/.claude/skills/bug-triaging/resources/templates/micro-sprint.md:43` and `head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:219`. **Required Fix:** (1) Add file-not-found shapes to `NOT_A_RED_PATTERNS`: `cannot open`, `No such file or directory`, `file or directory not found`, `can.t open file`, `ERROR: not found:`; (2) treat exit 2 from `sh`/`python` and exit 4 from `pytest` as "usage" when the output names a missing path; (3) make `--test-file` part of the prescribed invocation in the micro-sprint template and the review skill, or derive it from the micro-sprint's `Test file:` line and refuse to run without it; (4) add a bats case for the default path with the file absent at red (expected exit 4).

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:227` — `link_deps` symlinks the live tree's `.venv`, `node_modules`, `vendor`, `target` and `.tox` into each worktree by default; an editable Python install (`pip install -e`, `uv sync`, `poetry install` default) puts a `.pth` or `__editable__` finder in `.venv/…/site-packages` that names the live tree's `src/` by absolute path, and npm/pnpm/yarn workspace links resolve relative to the real `node_modules` in the live tree, so the red and green worktrees import the live tree's code, not the checked-out commit's.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:227` (the `ln -s`), `:222` (`link_deps`), `:27` (the header promise it breaks)
**Issue:** Reproduced with a src-layout project, a venv whose site-packages holds a `.pth` pointing at `$MAIN/src`, a red commit with the failing test and buggy source, a green commit that contains no fix, and the fix present only as an uncommitted edit in the live tree:

red-test-check: the test passes at the red commit: it does not reproduce the bug

pkg from /…/repo/src/pkg/__init__.py        <- the LIVE tree, not the worktree
verdict: DECOY             (exit 3)

Amend the header sentence at `:27` to state the remaining caveat precisely.
